children: *South Korea Proposes Biggest-Ever Budget Increase Next Year
*South Korea's 2027 Budget Calls for 12.8% Increase in Government Spending
South Korea Plans Record Budget Increase in 2027
South Korea's government has proposed a record increase in budget spending next year to boost weakening growth potential, backed by an expected surge in tax revenue.

The budget, reported to a cabinet meeting on Tuesday by the Ministry of Finance and Economy, calls for a 12.8% increase in national government spending to 820.9 trillion won, equivalent $600.38 billion, for 2027.
That would surpass the previous record annual budget increase of 10.6% in 2009, the ministry said.

South Korea faces structural challenges to its growth potential, with its low birth rate and rapidly aging population weighing on productivity. Intensifying global competition is also adding to the pressure.
The largest-ever fiscal spending plan aims to revive weakening potential growth as structurally low growth becomes entrenched, the ministry said.
The government also plans to use the planned spending to ensure that the benefits of the recent artificial-intelligence-driven semiconductor boom are more widely shared.

The budget includes a major spending boost for new growth engines such as AI infrastructure build-out as well as research and development in semiconductors, autonomous driving and next-generation space rockets.

The government plans to create a "future response" state fund to finance those projects and cover potential additional fiscal spending ahead, as it expects sizable increases in corporate and income tax revenue amid brisk chip exports driven by the AI boom, the ministry said.
It added that the government plans to repay more debt than previously planned while reducing treasury issuance.
The national debt is expected to fall to 48.3% of gross domestic product in 2027 from 51.6% in 2026. The fiscal deficit is forecast to narrow to 0.1% of GDP next year from 3.9% this year.
The budget plan is subject to approval by the National Assembly, which is the South Korean legislature controlled by the ruling party.
